restatements.text: Requires voters to show a current government-issued photo ID at the polling place before receiving a ballot.
Allows voters without ID to cast a provisional ballot, which will be counted only if they present identification to the county clerk within six days after the election.

analysis.answer: Under current law, voters verify their identity by stating their name and address and signing a poll book. This clause changes the process to require presenting a current government-issued photo ID.

Direct costs include administrative expenses for processing provisional ballots. Opportunity costs include the time and transportation required for voters to travel to the county clerk's office within the six-day window.

The costs fall on voters who do not currently possess a valid government-issued photo ID and must spend time obtaining one. The benefits accrue to individuals and organizations prioritizing stricter in-person identity verification at the polls.

Political campaigns and advocacy groups will likely shift resources toward educating voters about ID requirements and organizing efforts to help provisional voters cure their ballots during the six-day window.

It addresses the potential for in-person voter impersonation by requiring a photo ID. However, it creates a barrier to entry for voters who lack qualifying identification or face hurdles obtaining it.
County clerks gain the administrative duty and discretion to verify IDs presented during the six-day post-election period and determine if provisional ballots may be counted.

flags.note: The text does not specify which levels of government (e.g., federal, state, local, tribal) or institutions (e.g., state universities) qualify as issuers of the identification.

items.text: Stricter identity verification steps before a ballot is issued at the polling place.
A post-election verification process requiring ID before provisional ballots are counted.
The ability to receive a ballot without possessing and presenting a specific photo ID.
The ability to finalize voting on election day without needing to travel to the county clerk later if ID is forgotten.
